name: VA-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Walkinshaw with massive financial advantage ($2.8M raised vs ~$11K)
model.rationale: The baseline's D+24.4 margin rests on a D+18 district, incumbency, and an overwhelming money gap, with no evidence pointing the other way. Prediction markets at 97% Democratic confirm Safe D status.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a dramatically tighter race or unexpected incumbent scandal would be the only plausible trigger for revision.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern Virginia's 11th District is solidly Democratic, with a partisan lean of D+18, and incumbent James Walkinshaw is running for a full term after winning the seat. He holds an enormous resource advantage, having raised about $2.8 million with nearly $1 million on hand, while Republican Arthur Purves has raised roughly $11,000. Outside spending also heavily favors Walkinshaw.

There are no public general-election polls or expert ratings for this race, so the forecast relies on district fundamentals, the financial imbalance, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at about 97 percent. All available evidence points to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty being the exact size of the margin rather than the outcome.
